name: CI python

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-python-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # EVERY PR AND MAIN PUSH RUNS THIS WORKFLOW; the path filter lives in
  # this job, not on the trigger, because `python-checks` below is a
  # REQUIRED CHECK and a required check has to be produced on every PR
  # (AGENT.md, "Required checks run on every PR"). A job skipped by
  # `if:` reports `skipped`, which the ruleset accepts.
  changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      python: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.python }}
      codec: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.codec }}
      codec-source: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.codec-source }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            python:
              - "pyhoglake/**"
              - "pyhoglake-variant-codec/**"
              - "hedgerow/**"
              - "millrace/**"
              - "bench/**"
              # The uv workspace root: one lock for all four trees.
              - "pyproject.toml"
              - "uv.lock"
              # The OpenAPI spec is the wire contract the clients
              # conform to.
              - "server/src/main/resources/openapi/hoglake.yaml"
              # Server files the client's parity tests parse, so that a
              # server-only change to them reds here rather than on the
              # next unrelated pyhoglake PR: test_variant_ddl.py reads
              # VariantShredding.kt's limits, vocabularies and column
              # messages, ColumnTrees.kt's container message (ops.py
              # raises it), Identifiers.kt's cap, Model.kt's ColType
              # vocabulary (as test_transforms.py and test_nested.py
              # read Model.kt too), and the request seeds of the
              # shredding fuzz corpus (its JDK check also reads
              # build.gradle.kts and the Dockerfile, which change with
              # every dependency bump and are left out: only a JDK
              # downgrade could red that check). dependabot.yml is in the
              # filter too:
              # test_pyarrow_floor.test_the_latest_pyarrow_canary_keeps_the_dependency_cooldown
              # holds the pyarrow canary's cooldown to its uv cooldown.
              - "server/src/main/kotlin/com/posthog/hoglake/model/Model.kt"
              - "server/src/main/kotlin/com/posthog/hoglake/service/VariantShredding.kt"
              - "server/src/main/kotlin/com/posthog/hoglake/service/ColumnTrees.kt"
              - "server/src/main/kotlin/com/posthog/hoglake/service/Identifiers.kt"
              - "server/src/test/resources/com/posthog/hoglake/fuzz/VariantShreddingFuzzTestInputs/**"
              - ".github/dependabot.yml"
              - ".github/workflows/ci-python.yml"
              - ".github/workflows/pyhoglake-checks.yml"
              - ".github/workflows/python-live.yml"
              - ".github/workflows/variant-codec-wheels.yml"
              - "ci/**"
            # What the codec's wheels are built and tested from, the
            # lock (pyarrow, the test env) included.
            codec:
              - "pyhoglake-variant-codec/**"
              - "uv.lock"
              - ".github/workflows/variant-codec-wheels.yml"
              - "ci/variant-codec-wheel.sh"
              - "ci/variant_codec_smoke.py"
            # What a codec release is built from.
            codec-source:
              - "pyhoglake-variant-codec/src/**"
              - "pyhoglake-variant-codec/Cargo.*"
              - "pyhoglake-variant-codec/pyproject.toml"
              - "pyhoglake-variant-codec/rust-toolchain.toml"

  # THE GATE, and the check the ruleset requires. It is this job and not
  # `pyhoglake`, `check` or `millrace` so that the live client suites (run inside
  # pyhoglake-checks) cannot be red on a PR that merges: #304 wired the
  # live suites in while they were failing and merged on a ruleset that
  # required only the leaf jobs, and main was red for two hours until
  # #306. A gate that is not required is a comment.
  # Runs (and fails) when `changes` itself failed: a skipped gate
  # passes the ruleset, so a broken filter must not read as "nothing
  # to check".
  # The codec's wheels are gated only when the codec changed, and its
  # version check only on a PR that changes its source.
  python-checks:
    if: always() && (needs.changes.result != 'success' || needs.changes.outputs.python == 'true')
    needs: [changes, pyhoglake, check, millrace, variant-codec-wheels, codec-version]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Require Python checks and live suites
        env:
          CHANGES_RESULT: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          CLIENT_RESULT: ${{ needs.pyhoglake.result }}
          OTHER_RESULT: ${{ needs.check.result }}
          MILLRACE_RESULT: ${{ needs.millrace.result }}
          WHEELS_RESULT: ${{ needs.variant-codec-wheels.result }}
          CODEC_CHANGED: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.codec }}
          VERSION_RESULT: ${{ needs.codec-version.result }}
        run: |
          test "$CHANGES_RESULT" = success &&
            test "$CLIENT_RESULT" = success &&
            test "$OTHER_RESULT" = success &&
            test "$MILLRACE_RESULT" = success &&
            { test "$VERSION_RESULT" = success || test "$VERSION_RESULT" = skipped; } &&
            { test "$WHEELS_RESULT" = success ||
              { test "$CODEC_CHANGED" != true && test "$WHEELS_RESULT" = skipped; }; }

  pyhoglake:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.python == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/pyhoglake-checks.yml

  # The codec's manylinux wheels and sdist, each tested on its platform;
  # the artifacts stay on the run for later PRs to use. The other
  # platforms build on a release tag, or a manual run of
  # publish-pyhoglake-variant-codec.yml (design-native-encoder section 6).
  variant-codec-wheels:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.codec == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/variant-codec-wheels.yml
    with:
      all-platforms: false

  # A codec change ships under a version not yet released: a new one, or
  # a .dev one (pyhoglake's extra pins exact codec releases).
  codec-version:
    needs: changes
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.codec-source == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 2 # the PR's merge commit and the base, its first parent
      - name: A codec change has a new or .dev version
        run: |
          version() { git show "$1:pyhoglake-variant-codec/pyproject.toml" | grep -m1 '^version = ' | cut -d'"' -f2; }
          new=$(version HEAD) old=$(version HEAD^1)
          [ -n "$new" ] && [ -n "$old" ] || { echo "::error::cannot read the codec's version"; exit 1; }
          case "$new" in *.dev*) exit 0 ;; esac
          if [ "$new" = "$old" ]; then
            echo "::error::pyhoglake-variant-codec changed but is still $new: bump its version, or make it .dev"
            exit 1
          fi

  check:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.python == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - component: hedgerow
            lint: "true"
          # bench passes `ruff check` but carries a formatting backlog;
          # lint joins when that lands as its own diff (AGENT.md open
          # items).
          - component: bench
            lint: "false"
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.component }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - run: uv sync --locked

      - name: Lint (ruff, pinned in dev deps)
        if: matrix.lint == 'true'
        run: |
          uv run ruff check .
          uv run ruff format --check .

      # The reusable pyhoglake checks run both clients against a live stack.
      - name: Tests
        run: uv run pytest -m "not integration" -q

  millrace:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.python == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: millrace
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3

      - run: uv sync --locked

      - name: Lint (ruff, pinned in dev deps)
        run: |
          uv run ruff check .
          uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Type check (mypy)
        run: uv run mypy

      # Phase 2 integration tests (file:/// SlateDB: hard-kill
      # durability, contested-open fencing) need no services, so the
      # whole suite runs here; the LIVE docker stack suite (tests/live/,
      # marker `live`) is deselected by tests/conftest.py and runs
      # through ci/live-millrace.sh in the reusable python-live.yml
      # workflow (the `live-millrace` job). Benches stay deselected
      # (non-gating; conftest drops the bench marker without --bench).
      - name: Tests
        run: uv run pytest -q

      # M8: mutation-test the pure core (keyspace.py + planner.py — the
      # [tool.mutmut] scope) on every millrace change. Clean-slate:
      # mutmut 3.8's incremental stats go stale on function renames
      # (tests/MUTATION_TESTING.md), so `mutants/` is deleted first; a
      # full run is ~4 min here, well inside this job's budget, so no
      # incremental mode. The survivors gate (tests/check_mutants.py)
      # fails on any survivor the ledger does not name.
      - name: Mutation tests (pure core) + survivors gate
        run: |
          rm -rf mutants
          uv run mutmut run
          uv run python tests/check_mutants.py

# Kafka overlay for ci/live-millrace.sh — merged over
# server/docker-compose.yml with a second -f flag so the dev stack and
# ci/live-python.sh stay kafka-free. Single-node KRaft, reachable from
# the host on 127.0.0.1:${HOGLAKE_KAFKA_PORT:-29092} only.
#
# The image is pinned BY DIGEST (the lesson of millpond's `:latest`
# substitution, tests/hoglake_stack/stack.py): a tag is a pointer, and a
# live suite green against a broker nobody chose proves nothing. 3.9.0
# is the version millpond's stacks run; the digest is that tag's
# multi-arch manifest digest.
services:
  kafka:
    image: apache/kafka:3.9.0@sha256:fbc7d7c428e3755cf36518d4976596002477e4c052d1f80b5b9eafd06d0fff2f
    environment:
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: 1
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@localhost:29093
      # Empty-host listener form, per the apache/kafka image's own
      # compose examples — the docker wrapper's storage-format step
      # rejects 0.0.0.0 outright.
      KAFKA_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:29093,HOST://:29092
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092,HOST://127.0.0.1:${HOGLAKE_KAFKA_PORT:-29092}
      KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT,CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,HOST:PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: CONTROLLER
      KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE: "false"
      CLUSTER_ID: MkU3OEVBNTcwNTJENDM2Qk
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${HOGLAKE_KAFKA_PORT:-29092}:29092"
    healthcheck:
      test: /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 12

  # S3 latency injection for the stage store (tests/live/
  # test_live_stage_latency.py): the test creates a proxy listening on
  # :9100 with upstream minio:9000 through the admin API (:8474) and adds
  # a latency toxic, so the stage's object store sees S3-like round
  # trips while the lake stays direct. Pinned by digest (the 2.12.0
  # multi-arch manifest list), like kafka above.
  toxiproxy:
    image: ghcr.io/shopify/toxiproxy:2.12.0@sha256:9378ed52a28bc50edc1350f936f518f31fa95f0d15917d6eb40b8e376d1a214e
    depends_on:
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${HOGLAKE_TOXIPROXY_API_PORT:-28474}:8474"
      - "127.0.0.1:${HOGLAKE_TOXIPROXY_PORT:-29100}:9100"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "/toxiproxy-cli", "list"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 2s
      retries: 15

package com.posthog.hoglake.api

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper
import com.posthog.hoglake.App
import com.posthog.hoglake.Config
import com.posthog.hoglake.model.ColType
import com.posthog.hoglake.model.ColumnDef
import com.posthog.hoglake.service.CatalogService
import com.posthog.hoglake.testing.PgTestSupport
import io.ktor.client.request.get
import io.ktor.client.statement.bodyAsText
import io.ktor.http.HttpStatusCode
import io.ktor.server.testing.testApplication
import org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat
import org.jdbi.v3.core.Handle
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Tag
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

@Tag("integration")
class StorageUsageApiIntegrationTest {
    private val json = ObjectMapper()

    @Test
    fun `exact footprint includes history dropped tables and deletion vectors but not other catalogs`() {
        PgTestSupport.freshDatabase().use { db ->
            val catalogs = CatalogService(db.jdbi)
            val catalog = catalogs.createCatalog("footprint", "s3://footprint")
            catalogs.createNamespace("footprint", "ns")
            val table = catalogs.createTable("footprint", "ns", "events", listOf(ColumnDef("id", ColType.LONG)))
            val dropped = catalogs.createTable("footprint", "ns", "dropped", listOf(ColumnDef("id", ColType.LONG)))
            val other = catalogs.createCatalog("other", "s3://other")
            catalogs.createNamespace("other", "ns")
            val otherTable = catalogs.createTable("other", "ns", "events", listOf(ColumnDef("id", ColType.LONG)))
            val large = 9_007_199_254_740_993L
            db.jdbi.useHandle<Exception> { h ->
                dataFile(h, catalog.catalogId, table.tableId, 1, large)
                dataFile(h, catalog.catalogId, table.tableId, 2, 31, end = 3)
                dataFile(h, catalog.catalogId, dropped.tableId, 3, 41)
                dataFile(h, other.catalogId, otherTable.tableId, 1, 9999)
                h.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO hog_delete_file
                        (catalog_id, delete_file_id, table_id, data_file_id,
                         begin_snapshot, end_snapshot, path, delete_count, file_size_bytes)
                    VALUES (?, 1, ?, 1, 2, 3, 's3://footprint/old.puffin', 1, 5),
                           (?, 2, ?, 1, 3, NULL, 's3://footprint/new.puffin', 1, 7)
                    """,
                    catalog.catalogId,
                    table.tableId,
                    catalog.catalogId,
                    table.tableId,
                )
                h.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO hog_delete_file
                        (catalog_id, delete_file_id, table_id, data_file_id,
                         begin_snapshot, path, delete_count, file_size_bytes)
                    VALUES (?, 1, ?, 1, 2, 's3://other/delete.puffin', 1, 17)
                    """,
                    other.catalogId,
                    otherTable.tableId,
                )
                // Two undrained rows for the SAME path must both count. Claims/staging
                // also count, while every settled outcome is absent from the queue.
                h.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO hog_file_removal (catalog_id, path, file_kind, reason)
                    VALUES (?, 's3://footprint/queued.parquet', 'data', 'snapshot_expiry'),
                           (?, 's3://footprint/queued.parquet', 'data', 'table_drop_gc'),
                           (?, 's3://other/queued.parquet', 'data', 'snapshot_expiry')
                    """,
                    catalog.catalogId,
                    catalog.catalogId,
                    other.catalogId,
                )
                h.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO hog_file_removal
                        (catalog_id, path, file_kind, reason, claimed_at, claimed_by)
                    VALUES (?, 's3://footprint/staging.parquet', 'data',
                            'compaction_staging', now(), 'test-worker')
                    """,
                    catalog.catalogId,
                )
                for (outcome in listOf("deleted", "absent", "registered")) {
                    h.execute(
                        """
                        INSERT INTO hog_file_removal
                            (catalog_id, path, file_kind, reason, drained_at, drained_outcome)
                        VALUES (?, ?, 'data', 'compaction_staging', now(), ?)
                        """,
                        catalog.catalogId,
                        "s3://footprint/$outcome.parquet",
                        outcome,
                    )
                }
            }
            catalogs.dropTable(
                "footprint",
                "ns",
                "dropped",
                dropped.tableUuid,
                author = "integration-test",
                message = "drop table fixture",
            )
            val app = App.build(Config(hydratorIntervalMs = 0, metricsIntervalMs = 0), db.jdbi)
            testApplication {
                application { app.module(this) }
                val response = client.get("/v1/catalogs/footprint/storage-usage")
                assertThat(response.status).isEqualTo(HttpStatusCode.OK)
                assertUsage(json.readTree(response.bodyAsText()), (large + 84).toString(), "3")
                assertUsage(
                    json.readTree(client.get("/v1/catalogs/other/storage-usage").bodyAsText()),
                    "10016",
                    "1",
                )

                // Manifest removal, not physical object deletion, stops tracking a file.
                db.jdbi.useHandle<Exception> { h ->
                    h.execute("DELETE FROM hog_data_file WHERE catalog_id = ? AND data_file_id = 2", catalog.catalogId)
                    h.execute(
                        "DELETE FROM hog_delete_file WHERE catalog_id = ? AND delete_file_id = 1",
                        catalog.catalogId,
                    )
                    h.execute(
                        """
                        UPDATE hog_file_removal SET drained_at = now(), drained_outcome = 'deleted'
                        WHERE catalog_id = ? AND claimed_by = 'test-worker'
                        """,
                        catalog.catalogId,
                    )
                }
                assertUsage(
                    json.readTree(client.get("/v1/catalogs/footprint/storage-usage").bodyAsText()),
                    (large + 48).toString(),
                    "2",
                )
                for (query in listOf("snapshot=0", "at_timestamp=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")) {
                    assertThat(client.get("/v1/catalogs/footprint/storage-usage?$query").status)
                        .isEqualTo(HttpStatusCode.BadRequest)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `empty is zero while unknown and backend failure are errors`() {
        PgTestSupport.freshDatabase().use { db ->
            CatalogService(db.jdbi).createCatalog("empty", "s3://empty")
            val app = App.build(Config(hydratorIntervalMs = 0, metricsIntervalMs = 0), db.jdbi)
            testApplication {
                application { app.module(this) }
                val empty = client.get("/v1/catalogs/empty/storage-usage")
                assertThat(empty.status).isEqualTo(HttpStatusCode.OK)
                assertUsage(json.readTree(empty.bodyAsText()), "0", "0")
                for (catalog in listOf("unknown", "invalid'name")) {
                    val missing = client.get("/v1/catalogs/$catalog/storage-usage")
                    assertThat(missing.status).isEqualTo(HttpStatusCode.NotFound)
                    assertThat(json.readTree(missing.bodyAsText()).has("tracked_bytes")).isFalse()
                }
                db.dataSource.close()
                val failed = client.get("/v1/catalogs/empty/storage-usage")
                assertThat(failed.status).isEqualTo(HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError)
                assertThat(json.readTree(failed.bodyAsText()).has("tracked_bytes")).isFalse()
            }
        }
    }

    @Test
    fun `int64 overflow fails rather than silently truncating bytes`() {
        PgTestSupport.freshDatabase().use { db ->
            val catalogs = CatalogService(db.jdbi)
            val catalog = catalogs.createCatalog("overflow", "s3://overflow")
            catalogs.createNamespace("overflow", "ns")
            val table = catalogs.createTable("overflow", "ns", "events", listOf(ColumnDef("id", ColType.LONG)))
            db.jdbi.useHandle<Exception> { h ->
                dataFile(h, catalog.catalogId, table.tableId, 1, Long.MAX_VALUE)
                dataFile(h, catalog.catalogId, table.tableId, 2, 1)
            }
            val app = App.build(Config(hydratorIntervalMs = 0, metricsIntervalMs = 0), db.jdbi)
            testApplication {
                application { app.module(this) }
                val failed = client.get("/v1/catalogs/overflow/storage-usage")
                assertThat(failed.status).isEqualTo(HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError)
                assertThat(json.readTree(failed.bodyAsText()).has("tracked_bytes")).isFalse()
            }
        }
    }

    private fun assertUsage(
        body: JsonNode,
        bytes: String,
        pending: String,
    ) {
        assertThat(body.fieldNames().asSequence().toList())
            .containsExactlyInAnyOrder("tracked_bytes", "pending_delete_files")
        assertThat(body["tracked_bytes"].isTextual).isTrue()
        assertThat(body["pending_delete_files"].isTextual).isTrue()
        assertThat(body["tracked_bytes"].asText()).isEqualTo(bytes)
        assertThat(body["pending_delete_files"].asText()).isEqualTo(pending)
    }

    private fun dataFile(
        h: Handle,
        catalogId: Long,
        tableId: Long,
        fileId: Long,
        bytes: Long,
        end: Long? = null,
    ) {
        h.createUpdate(
            """
            INSERT INTO hog_data_file
                (catalog_id, data_file_id, table_id, begin_snapshot, end_snapshot,
                 path, record_count, file_size_bytes, row_id_start)
            VALUES (:catalog, :file, :table, 2, :end, :path, 2, :bytes, :row)
            """,
        ).bind("catalog", catalogId).bind("table", tableId).bind("file", fileId)
            .bind("end", end).bind("path", "s3://test/$catalogId/$fileId.parquet")
            .bind("bytes", bytes).bind("row", (fileId - 1) * 2).execute()
    }
}

"""Scenario 10 (Phase 5): compaction observation.

After a skewed run leaves a bucket of small age-triggered files, the
server's maintenance trigger (``POST /v1/catalogs/{c}/maintenance/compact``,
the same path the background loop drives — the loop is OFF in this
harness so the trigger is the only sweeper) rolls the small files up:
one group, six inputs, one output. The table stays queryable throughout
and the row counts stay EXACT — compaction changes no visible row.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

import livekit
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import pytest
from livekit import now_us

pytestmark = pytest.mark.live

TEAM = 5
WAVES = 6
PER_WAVE = 10
FLUSH_DEADLINE_S = 2


async def test_compaction_rolls_up_small_files(
    lake_home, topic_factory, producer_factory, admin
):
    table = lake_home.create_events_table()
    topic = topic_factory(partitions=2)
    producer = producer_factory(topic.name)

    cfg = livekit.live_config(
        topic=topic.name,
        group=topic.group,
        stage_base_path=f"stage/{livekit.RUN_ID}/{lake_home.slug}",
        catalog=lake_home.catalog.name,
        namespace="ns1",
        table=table.name,
        flush_deadline_s=FLUSH_DEADLINE_S,
        flush_sweep_s=1,
    )
    async with livekit.Pipeline(cfg, sweep_s=0.5):
        # Six waves, each its own flush → six small files in one
        # (team, month) bucket.
        seq = 0
        for wave in range(WAVES):
            base = now_us()
            await asyncio.to_thread(
                livekit.produce_batch,
                producer,
                [(TEAM, base + i) for i in range(PER_WAVE)],
                seq_start=seq,
            )
            seq += PER_WAVE
            want = wave + 1
            await livekit.wait_until_async(
                lambda w=want: len(livekit.lake_files(table, lake_home.head())) == w,
                60,
                desc=f"wave {wave} flushed ({wave + 1} files)",
            )

        files = livekit.lake_files(table, lake_home.head())
        assert len(files) == WAVES
        assert all(f.stats_state for f in files)

        # The compact sweep's candidate read wants hydrated stats (the
        # age flushes registered deferred) — the harness runs the
        # hydrator at 1s.
        await livekit.wait_until_async(
            lambda: all(
                f.stats_state == "provided"
                for f in livekit.lake_files(table, lake_home.head())
            ),
            60,
            desc="the hydrator backfilling deferred stats",
        )

        # Trigger one compaction sweep (the loop is off in this harness).
        result = await asyncio.to_thread(
            lake_home.client._request,
            "POST",
            f"/catalogs/{lake_home.catalog.name}/maintenance/compact",
        )
        assert result["groups_compacted"] == 1, result
        assert result["files_in"] == WAVES, result
        assert result["files_out"] == 1, result
        assert result["failed_groups"] == 0, result

        # The bucket rolled up; the table stays queryable with EXACT counts.
        head = lake_home.head()
        files_after = livekit.lake_files(table, head)
        assert len(files_after) == 1, [f.path for f in files_after]
        assert files_after[0].record_count == WAVES * PER_WAVE
        counts = livekit.lake_team_counts(table, head)
        assert counts == {TEAM: WAVES * PER_WAVE}

        # Full readback of the compacted output: exactly the produced seqs.
        data = await asyncio.to_thread(
            pq.read_table,
            files_after[0].path[len("s3://") :],
            filesystem=lake_home.fs,
        )
        assert data.num_rows == WAVES * PER_WAVE
        assert set(data.column("seq").to_pylist()) == set(range(WAVES * PER_WAVE))

"""The client's side of hoglake authentication, against in-process fakes."""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import threading
import types

import httpx
import pytest

from pyhoglake import BearerToken, ClientCredentials, HoglakeClient, HoglakeError
from pyhoglake.client import USER_AGENT


class Fakes:
    """A token endpoint and a hoglake that accepts exactly one token."""

    def __init__(self, expires_in: int = 900) -> None:
        self.expires_in = expires_in
        self.mints = 0
        self.accepted = "t1"
        self.token_status = 200
        self.token_requests: list[httpx.Request] = []
        self.api_auth: list[str | None] = []

    def token(self, request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        self.token_requests.append(request)
        if self.token_status != 200:
            return httpx.Response(self.token_status, json={"error": "invalid_client"})
        self.mints += 1
        return httpx.Response(
            200,
            json={
                "access_token": f"t{self.mints}",
                "token_type": "Bearer",
                "expires_in": self.expires_in,
            },
        )

    def api(self, request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        auth = request.headers.get("authorization")
        self.api_auth.append(auth)
        assert request.headers["user-agent"] == USER_AGENT
        if auth != f"Bearer {self.accepted}":
            return httpx.Response(
                401,
                json={"error": "unknown_key"},
                headers={"WWW-Authenticate": 'Bearer error="unknown_key"'},
            )
        return httpx.Response(200, json=[])

    def credentials(self) -> ClientCredentials:
        return ClientCredentials(
            "http://issuer/oauth/token",
            "hlc_test",
            "s3cret",
            http=httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(self.token)),
        )

    def client(self) -> HoglakeClient:
        client = HoglakeClient("http://hoglake", auth=self.credentials())
        client._http._transport = httpx.MockTransport(self.api)
        return client


def test_a_minted_token_is_attached_and_reused() -> None:
    fakes = Fakes()
    with fakes.client() as client:
        client._request("GET", "/catalogs")
        client._request("GET", "/catalogs")
    assert fakes.mints == 1
    assert fakes.api_auth == ["Bearer t1", "Bearer t1"]
    minted = fakes.token_requests[0]
    assert (
        minted.headers["authorization"]
        == "Basic " + base64.b64encode(b"hlc_test:s3cret").decode()
    )
    assert minted.content == b"grant_type=client_credentials&audience=hoglake"


def test_a_refused_token_is_replaced_once_and_the_request_retried() -> None:
    fakes = Fakes()
    with fakes.client() as client:
        client._request("GET", "/catalogs")
        fakes.accepted = "t2"
        client._request("GET", "/catalogs")
    assert fakes.api_auth == ["Bearer t1", "Bearer t1", "Bearer t2"]


def test_a_second_401_is_not_retried_again() -> None:
    fakes = Fakes()
    fakes.accepted = "never"
    with fakes.client() as client, pytest.raises(HoglakeError):
        client._request("GET", "/catalogs")
    assert len(fakes.api_auth) == 2


def test_a_failing_token_endpoint_raises_without_calling_the_api() -> None:
    fakes = Fakes()
    fakes.token_status = 401
    with fakes.client() as client, pytest.raises(HoglakeError, match="token endpoint"):
        client._request("GET", "/catalogs")
    assert fakes.api_auth == []


def test_a_fixed_bearer_token() -> None:
    fakes = Fakes()
    client = HoglakeClient("http://hoglake", auth=BearerToken("t1"))
    client._http._transport = httpx.MockTransport(fakes.api)
    with client:
        client._request("GET", "/catalogs")
    assert fakes.api_auth == ["Bearer t1"]


class Clock:
    """Stands in for ``time`` inside pyhoglake.auth, which only reads monotonic()."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.now = 1000.0

    def monotonic(self) -> float:
        return self.now


@pytest.fixture
def clock(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Clock:
    fake = Clock()
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "pyhoglake.auth.time", types.SimpleNamespace(monotonic=fake.monotonic)
    )
    return fake


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("expires_in", "refresh_after"),
    [
        # Long-lived: refreshed 60s before expiry.
        (900, 840.0),
        # Short-lived: the margin is capped at a fifth of the lifetime.
        (100, 80.0),
    ],
)
def test_a_token_is_reused_until_its_refresh_point_then_reminted(
    clock: Clock, expires_in: int, refresh_after: float
) -> None:
    fakes = Fakes(expires_in=expires_in)
    creds = fakes.credentials()
    assert creds._current() == "t1"
    clock.now += refresh_after - 0.001
    assert creds._current() == "t1"
    clock.now += 0.001
    assert creds._current() == "t2"
    assert fakes.mints == 2


def test_threads_that_find_the_token_stale_together_mint_once() -> None:
    threads = 8
    fakes = Fakes()
    creds = fakes.credentials()

    # Count arrivals at the lock, and hold the one mint until every thread has
    # arrived, so all of them have seen the token missing before it exists.
    real_lock = creds._lock
    arrivals = threading.Semaphore(0)

    class CountingLock:
        def __enter__(self) -> None:
            arrivals.release()
            real_lock.acquire()

        def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
            real_lock.release()

    creds._lock = CountingLock()  # type: ignore[assignment]
    mint = fakes.token

    def held_mint(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        if fakes.mints == 0:
            for _ in range(threads):
                assert arrivals.acquire(timeout=5), "not every thread reached the lock"
        return mint(request)

    fakes.token = held_mint  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    creds._http = httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(fakes.token))

    tokens: list[str] = []
    workers = [
        threading.Thread(target=lambda: tokens.append(creds._current()))
        for _ in range(threads)
    ]
    for worker in workers:
        worker.start()
    for worker in workers:
        worker.join(timeout=10)
    assert tokens == ["t1"] * threads
    assert fakes.mints == 1

"""Hypothesis mutation-fuzzing of wire-model parsing and error mapping.

Claims under test:

* Unknown extra fields at any level are ignored (forward compat).
* Missing optionals parse to their defaults.
* Error responses (any status 400-599, any body JSON shape or raw
  bytes) always map to the right HoglakeError subclass, never crash the
  mapper, and always stringify.
* Missing REQUIRED fields / wrong-typed nested containers raise ONE
  typed client-side error — MalformedResponseError — naming the model
  and the offending field (bugs.md #24; formerly leaked KeyError,
  AttributeError, or TypeError depending on the model's parse style).

# A dataclass field with no default is wire-REQUIRED: the `_pick`-based
# `from_wire`s fail to construct without it, and the hand-written ones
# index it. Derived rather than restated, so a new model needs no entry
# here — with one override, for the hand-written `from_wire` that reads
# a no-default field with `.get` instead.
WIRE_OPTIONAL_DESPITE_NO_DEFAULT: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    # The writer path asks for identity only (`totals=false`), so a
    # getTable answer legitimately omits the three totals and they come
    # back None; `columns` has always been tolerated absent.
    "TableInfo": frozenset(
        {"columns", "record_count", "file_count", "file_size_bytes"}
    ),
}


def wire_required(cls: type) -> frozenset[str]:
    no_default = {
        f.name
        for f in dataclasses.fields(cls)
        if f.default is dataclasses.MISSING and f.default_factory is dataclasses.MISSING
    }
    return frozenset(
        no_default - WIRE_OPTIONAL_DESPITE_NO_DEFAULT.get(cls.__name__, frozenset())
    )

)


@MODEL_SETTINGS
@given(model_case)
def test_models_parse_with_extra_unknown_fields(case):
    cls, wire, extras = case
    # Extras must not shadow real fields -- and "real" means the MODEL's
    # fields, not the keys this particular `wire` happens to carry.
    # Filtering against `wire` let an OPTIONAL field's name through
    # whenever hypothesis omitted it: `partition_spec` is optional on
    # TableInfo, so an extras key by that literal name survived, shadowed
    # the real field with junk, and `from_wire` correctly raised. Rare
    # but reachable -- hypothesis harvests the literal from this source
    # -- and it is the test's premise that was wrong, not the model's
    # refusal.
    known = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(cls)} | set(wire)
    extras = {k: v for k, v in extras.items() if k not in known}
    polluted = {**wire, **extras}
    obj = cls.from_wire(polluted)
    clean = cls.from_wire(dict(wire))
    assert obj == clean  # unknown fields ignored, known fields identical

    parsed_specially = {

        "changes",
        "columns",
        "files",
        "delete_files",
        "partition_spec",
        "data_file",
        "delete_file",
        "partition_values",
    }
    for k, v in wire.items():
        if k in parsed_specially:
            continue
        assert getattr(obj, k) == v


# Regression (bugs.md #24, formerly an xfail BUG pin): a response
# missing a required field must raise MalformedResponseError — never a
# leaked KeyError (direct-index parsers) or TypeError (_pick parsers).
#
# PARAMETRIZED over (model, required field), not sampled. Two earlier
# shapes of this test were not gates: the original accepted EITHER
# outcome for every field, so a field that stopped being wire-required
# went unnoticed (which is what happened when the writer path made
# TableInfo's three totals optional); and splitting the two halves off
# `wire_required` while still drawing ONE victim per example left the
# defect showing on only about a quarter of seeds — a mutation making
# `TableInfo.namespace` optional reddened 5 of 20 runs, so 75% of CI
# passed with it in place. Dropping every required field of every model
# on every run is the only version that cannot flake.
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "case_index,victim",
    [
        (i, f)
        for i, (cls, _) in enumerate(MODEL_CASES)
        for f in sorted(wire_required(cls))
    ],
    ids=lambda v: str(v),
)
@given(st.data())
def test_missing_required_field_raises_malformed_response(case_index, victim, data):
    cls, strategy = MODEL_CASES[case_index]
    wire = data.draw(strategy)
    if victim not in wire:
        # The strategy declared it optional while the model requires it:
        # the two disagree, and that disagreement is itself the bug this
        # test exists to catch.
        raise AssertionError(
            f"{cls.__name__}.{victim} is wire-required but the strategy "
            "does not always generate it"
        )
    broken = {k: v for k, v in wire.items() if k != victim}
    with pytest.raises(MalformedResponseError) as excinfo:
        cls.from_wire(broken)
    # the one sanctioned parse error, naming the model
    assert cls.__name__ in str(excinfo.value)


@given(model_case, st.data())
def test_missing_optional_field_still_parses(case, data):
    """The other half: removing an OPTIONAL field parses cleanly, and
    anything but a clean parse (KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError...)
    propagates and fails."""
    cls, wire, _ = case
    optional = sorted(set(wire) - wire_required(cls))
    if not optional:
        return
    victim = data.draw(st.sampled_from(optional))
    cls.from_wire({k: v for k, v in wire.items() if k != victim})

@given(ISO)

    s = Snapshot.from_wire(
        {"snapshot_id": 1, "snapshot_time": iso, "schema_version": 1}

    assert s.snapshot_time.tzinfo is not None  # offset forms keep tz
    assert s.snapshot_time.year == 2026


def test_changes_and_files_default_to_empty_tuples():
    s = Snapshot.from_wire(
        {"snapshot_id": 1, "snapshot_time": "2026-09-04T12:00:00Z", "schema_version": 1}
    )
    assert s.changes == ()
    p = ChangesPlan.from_wire({"table_uuid": "u", "from_snapshot": 1, "to_snapshot": 2})
    assert p.files == () and p.delete_files == ()
    # explicit null arrays behave like absent ones
    p2 = ChangesPlan.from_wire(
        {
            "table_uuid": "u",
            "from_snapshot": 1,
            "to_snapshot": 2,
            "files": None,
            "delete_files": None,
        }
    )

# -- ApiError mapping under fire -------------------------------------------

error_bodies = st.one_of(
    st.fixed_dictionaries({}, optional={"error": json_scalars, "detail": json_values}),
    json_values,  # non-dict JSON bodies
)


@MODEL_SETTINGS
@given(
    st.integers(400, 599),
    st.one_of(
        error_bodies.map(lambda b: ("json", b)),
        st.binary(max_size=64).map(lambda b: ("raw", b)),
        st.just(("raw", b"")),
    ),
    st.sampled_from([AlreadyExistsError, CommitConflictError]),
)
def test_error_mapping_total_and_correct(status, body, conflict_cls):
    kind, payload = body
    if kind == "json":
        resp = httpx.Response(status, json=payload)
    else:
        resp = httpx.Response(status, content=payload)
    with pytest.raises(HoglakeError) as ei:
        HoglakeClient._raise(resp, conflict_cls)
    exc = ei.value
    expected = {
        404: NotFoundError,
        409: conflict_cls,
        410: ExpiredError,
        422: ValidationError,
    }.get(status, HoglakeError)
    assert type(exc) is expected
    assert exc.status_code == status
    assert isinstance(str(exc), str)  # stringification never explodes
    # retryability contract: only commit conflicts retry
    assert exc.retryable is (status == 409 and conflict_cls is CommitConflictError)

"""Reject another server on the test port and incomplete startup responses."""

import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

CHECKER = Path(__file__).with_name("check_live_identity.py")


class LiveIdentityTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_only_the_expected_server_is_ready(self):
        for response, expected in (
            ('{"name": "this-run"}', 0),
            ('{"name": "other-run"}', 1),
            ("{}", 1),
            ("[]", 1),
            ("null", 1),
            ("", 1),
            ("not JSON", 1),
        ):
            with self.subTest(response=response):
                result = subprocess.run(
                    [sys.executable, str(CHECKER), "this-run"],
                    input=response,
                    check=False,
                    capture_output=True,
                    text=True,
                )
                self.assertEqual(result.returncode, expected, result.stderr)
                self.assertEqual(result.stderr, "")


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""Pin millrace's wiring into the ci-python.yml gate.

Phase 0's meta-test (docs/kafka-ingestion-plan.md): a workflow that
path-filters itself out of a PR leaves its required check "expected"
forever (AGENT.md, #299), and a gate that does not need a leaf job
cannot see that job fail (AGENT.md, #304). Both failure modes are
pinned here, and so are the image's hand-pinned codec build tools.
"""

import re
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WORKFLOWS = ROOT / ".github" / "workflows"
WORKFLOW = WORKFLOWS / "ci-python.yml"


def _jobs():
    return yaml.safe_load(WORKFLOW.read_text())["jobs"]


def test_millrace_tree_triggers_the_workflow():
    steps = _jobs()["changes"]["steps"]
    filter_step = next(step for step in steps if step.get("id") == "filter")
    filters = yaml.safe_load(filter_step["with"]["filters"])
    assert "millrace/**" in filters["python"]


def test_python_checks_gate_needs_the_millrace_job():
    jobs = _jobs()
    assert "millrace" in jobs
    assert "millrace" in jobs["python-checks"]["needs"]


def test_python_checks_gate_needs_the_codec_wheels_when_the_codec_changes():
    """The Rust codec's wheels (variant-codec-wheels.yml) run only when the
    codec changed, which runs the gate too, and the gate must see them fail."""
    jobs = _jobs()
    steps = jobs["changes"]["steps"]
    filter_step = next(step for step in steps if step.get("id") == "filter")
    filters = yaml.safe_load(filter_step["with"]["filters"])
    both = set(filters["python"]) & set(filters["codec"])
    assert {
        "pyhoglake-variant-codec/**",
        ".github/workflows/variant-codec-wheels.yml",
    } <= both
    assert "uv.lock" in filters["codec"]
    wheels = jobs["variant-codec-wheels"]
    assert wheels["if"] == "needs.changes.outputs.codec == 'true'"
    assert wheels["uses"] == "./.github/workflows/variant-codec-wheels.yml"
    assert wheels["with"] == {"all-platforms": False}
    assert "variant-codec-wheels" in jobs["python-checks"]["needs"]
    # A release builds every platform.
    publish = WORKFLOWS / "publish-pyhoglake-variant-codec.yml"
    release = yaml.safe_load(publish.read_text())["jobs"]["wheels"]
    assert release["with"] == {"all-platforms": True}


def test_python_checks_gate_needs_the_codec_version_check():
    """A codec change ships under a new or .dev version (pyhoglake's extra
    pins exact releases); the gate must see that check fail."""
    jobs = _jobs()
    steps = jobs["changes"]["steps"]
    filter_step = next(step for step in steps if step.get("id") == "filter")
    filters = yaml.safe_load(filter_step["with"]["filters"])
    assert "pyhoglake-variant-codec/src/**" in filters["codec-source"]
    assert "needs.changes.outputs.codec-source == 'true'" in jobs["codec-version"]["if"]
    assert "codec-version" in jobs["python-checks"]["needs"]
    gate = jobs["python-checks"]["steps"][0]
    assert "${{ needs.codec-version.result }}" in gate["env"].values()
    assert "$VERSION_RESULT" in gate["run"]


def test_the_image_builds_the_codec_with_the_release_wheels_tools():
    """millrace/Dockerfile's codec stage pins Rust by its image tag, and
    maturin and zig by version, by hand: they must be rust-toolchain.toml's
    and variant-codec-wheels.yml's, which build the published wheels."""
    dockerfile = (ROOT / "millrace" / "Dockerfile").read_text()
    toolchain = ROOT / "pyhoglake-variant-codec" / "rust-toolchain.toml"
    channel = tomllib.loads(toolchain.read_text())["toolchain"]["channel"]
    stage = r"^FROM --platform=\$BUILDPLATFORM rust:(\S+)-slim-\S+ AS codec$"
    assert re.findall(stage, dockerfile, re.MULTILINE) == [channel]
    env = yaml.safe_load((WORKFLOWS / "variant-codec-wheels.yml").read_text())["env"]
    for pin in (env["MATURIN"], env["ZIG"]):
        assert f" {pin} " in dockerfile
